cards.explanation: The answer is unfaithfulness. The writer says Judah was exiled to Babylon "…because of their unfaithfulness." (1 Chronicles 9:1) He says it plainly and doesn't dress it up. I think it's a hard line to read, so I'll just say it's heavy and leave it there.

The answer is priests and Levites. The first to resettle their own property in their cities were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants. (1 Chronicles 9:2) So the people who served at the house of God were among the first ones back, friends. The story didn't stay in Babylon.

The answer is False. Shallum and his relatives were assigned to guard the thresholds of the Tent "…just as their fathers had been assigned to guard the entrance to the dwelling of the LORD." (1 Chronicles 9:19) Their fathers had been assigned this very kind of guarding before them. So it's not a brand new job, bakers, it's a family tradition.

The answer is that the LORD was with him. The writer says Phinehas son of Eleazar had been in charge of the gatekeepers, "…and the LORD was with him." (1 Chronicles 9:20) Of everything the writer could say about a man, that's the line he picked. I'd take it over any title.

The answer is trust. David and Samuel the seer "…had appointed them to their positions of trust." (1 Chronicles 9:22) A seer is someone who sees. These gatekeepers were trusted with the doors of the house of the LORD, friends, and that's no small thing.

The answer is on all four sides. "The gatekeepers were stationed on the four sides: east, west, north, and south." (1 Chronicles 9:24) Every direction had gatekeepers standing at their posts. That's a whole lot of doorways covered, friends. So no side of the house of the LORD was left without a gatekeeper.

The answer is seven days. Their relatives "…came from their villages at fixed times to serve with them for seven-day periods." (1 Chronicles 9:25) A week at a time on the job, friends. Seven days is the answer.

The answer is that they guard it and open it each morning. The four chief gatekeepers spent the night around the house of God "…because they were responsible for guarding it and opening it every morning." (1 Chronicles 9:27) Guarding it and opening it were their jobs. I think that's one early alarm clock, and nobody could hit snooze on it.

The answer is True. Some of them were "…in charge of the articles used in worship, to count them whenever they were brought in or taken out." (1 Chronicles 9:28) Every item got counted going in and coming out. I'd have loved that system for my cookie cutters.

The answer is baking the bread! "A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with baking the bread." (1 Chronicles 9:31) Somebody was trusted to bake in the house of God, and I'm a little proud of the profession. Okay, a LOT proud.

The answer is that they are on duty day and night. The musicians stayed in the temple chambers and "…were exempt from other duties because they were on duty day and night." (1 Chronicles 9:33) Music was their whole assignment, friends. I think that's a lot of practicing.
